blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Abraham was old, and his son Isaac was not yet married. Abraham did not want Isaac to marry a woman from the land where they were living. So he sent his oldest servant all the way back to the land of his family to find a wife for his son.

verses.text: And the servant took ten camels of the camels of his master, and departed; for all the goods of his master were in his hand: and he arose, and went to Mesopotamia, unto the city of Nahor.

verses.text: And he made his camels to kneel down without the city by a well of water at the time of the evening, even the time that women go out to draw water.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: It was evening. The servant was a long way from home, standing at a strange well with ten thirsty camels. He did not know a single person in that town. So he prayed.

verses.text: And he said, O LORD God of my master Abraham, I pray thee, send me good speed this day, and shew kindness unto my master Abraham.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: It was a big thing to ask. Ten camels drink a lot of water after a long trip through the desert. A young woman who offered to water them all would be offering hours of hard work to a stranger.

verses.text: And it came to pass, before he had done speaking, that, behold, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham’s brother, with her pitcher upon her shoulder.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Back and forth she went, from the well to the trough, again and again, until every camel had its fill. Nobody made her do it. Kindness was simply who she was.

verses.text: And the man wondering at her held his peace, to wit whether the LORD had made his journey prosperous or not.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The servant watched her and did not say a word. He was waiting to see if this was really God's answer.

blocks.text: Bethuel. Nahor. These were Abraham's own family. Out of all the women in that town, the one who came to the well was a relative of his master.

verses.text: And he said, Blessed be the LORD God of my master Abraham, who hath not left destitute my master of his mercy and his truth: I being in the way, the LORD led me to the house of my master’s brethren.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The first thing the servant did was not to celebrate or make plans. He bowed his head right there by the well and thanked God. Rebekah would go on to marry Isaac and become a mother in the family of promise. It began with a prayer at a well, and a young woman who was kind to a stranger and his tired camels.

pastor.note: Faithful to Gen 24:10-27 (v16's description skipped, nothing changed); the servant's prayer and thanks kept as scripture; nothing invented about Rebekah beyond her kindness in the text.

cultural.note: Rebekah's kindness and work shown with dignity; no romance framing.
